subproblem.title: Limit of the left side: discrete integration by parts against a C^1 field
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) and L* := L(L, R) (operator norms). Let U ⊆ R^n be open, F : R^n -> L* of class C^1 on U, tau : R^n -> L continuous with compact support and tsupport tau ⊆ U, and e in R^n. Then ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx -> -∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx as h -> 0 with h ≠ 0 (along 𝓝[≠] 0), where DF(x)e := fderiv R F x e.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Rn n → ((Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (τ : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (U : Set (Rn n)) (e : Rn n), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F U → Continuous τ → HasCompactSupport τ → tsupport τ ⊆ U → Tendsto (fun h : ℝ => ∫ x in U, F x (h⁻¹ • (τ x - τ (x - h • e)))) (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 (-∫ x in U, fderiv ℝ F x e (τ x)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el (translation of the shifted term and passage to the limit on the left side), with F := DPsi o Du and tau := Dzeta abstracted. The uniform convergence of Step 7 is supplied by the sibling dohr_eb_ehs_del_diffquot_uniform.
Notation: K := tsupport tau; Q_h(y) := h^{-1}(F(y + he) - F(y)) in L*; DF(y)e := fderiv R F y e in L*. Lebesgue measure on R^n is translation invariant.
1. Margin. K is compact (tau has compact support) and K ⊆ U with U open, so there is delta > 0 with K' := cthickening delta K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put h0 := delta/(||e|| + 1) > 0; {h : |h| < h0} is a neighbourhood of 0. For |h| < h0 and y in K, dist(y + he, y) = |h| ||e|| < delta, so y + he lies in K' ⊆ U.
2. Basic facts. tau(y) = 0 for y not in K. F is continuous on U, and y -> DF(y)e is continuous on U (F is C^1 on the open U: ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, then evaluation at e). tau is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: ||tau(y)|| <= C_tau for all y. Since K is compact and y -> DF(y)e is continuous on K, ||DF(y)e|| <= C_D for y in K.
3. Uniform convergence (sibling). By dohr_eb_ehs_del_diffquot_uniform with E := L*, f := F, the open set U, the compact set K ⊆ U and the direction e: Q_h(y) -> DF(y)e uniformly for y in K as h -> 0, h ≠ 0.
4. The left side is minus an integral of Q_h. Fix h with 0 < |h| < h0.
   (a) The integrand x -> F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] vanishes for x outside U: then x is not in K, so tau(x) = 0; and x - he is not in K, since otherwise x = (x - he) + he would lie in K' ⊆ U by step 1. Hence its integral over U equals its integral over R^n (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
   (b) Integrability. y -> F(y)[tau(y)] is continuous on the compact set K (F is continuous on U ⊇ K, tau is continuous, evaluation is continuous) and vanishes off K, so it is integrable on R^n (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact, then IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). Likewise y -> F(y + he)[tau(y)] is continuous on K (because y + he lies in K' ⊆ U for y in K) and vanishes off K, hence is integrable; its translate x -> F(x)[tau(x - he)] is then integrable by translation invariance (Integrable.comp_sub_right).
   (c) By linearity of F(x), F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] = h^{-1}(F(x)[tau(x)] - F(x)[tau(x - he)]). With (b), the integral over R^n of the left side equals h^{-1}(∫ F(x)[tau(x)] dx - ∫ F(x)[tau(x - he)] dx).
   (d) Translation invariance (substitute x = y + he; integral_add_right_eq_self): ∫ F(x)[tau(x - he)] dx = ∫ F(y + he)[tau(y)] dy.
   (e) By (c), (d) and the integrability in (b): ∫ F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx = h^{-1} ∫ (F(y)[tau(y)] - F(y + he)[tau(y)]) dy = -∫ Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy. The last integrand vanishes off K, so together with (a):
       ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx = -∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy   for all 0 < |h| < h0.   (1)
5. The limit integral. y -> DF(y)e[tau(y)] vanishes on U \ K, so (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, K ⊆ U, U measurable)
       ∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx = ∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy.   (2)
6. Passage to the limit on K. By step 3 there is a punctured neighbourhood of 0 on which ||Q_h(y) - DF(y)e|| < 1 for every y in K; for such h and y in K, ||Q_h(y)|| <= ||DF(y)e|| + 1 <= C_D + 1, hence |Q_h(y)[tau(y)]| <= ||Q_h(y)|| ||tau(y)|| <= (C_D + 1) C_tau. Moreover:
   - for 0 < |h| < h0 the function y -> Q_h(y)[tau(y)] is continuous on K (y + he lies in U for y in K), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to the compact, measurable set K;
   - the constant (C_D + 1) C_tau is integrable on K, which has finite measure;
   - for every y in K, Q_h(y) -> DF(y)e (uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence), hence Q_h(y)[tau(y)] -> DF(y)e[tau(y)] (evaluation at tau(y) is a continuous linear map on L*).
   The filter 𝓝[≠] 0 is countably generated, so the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) gives
       ∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy -> ∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy   as h -> 0, h ≠ 0.   (3)
   (Equivalently, as in the parent proof, for small h one has |∫_K (Q_h(y) - DF(y)e)[tau(y)] dy| <= |K| C_tau sup_{y in K} ||Q_h(y) - DF(y)e||, which tends to 0 by step 3.)
7. Conclusion. By (1) the function h -> ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx agrees, on the punctured neighbourhood {0 < |h| < h0} of 0, with h -> -∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy, which by (3) and (2) tends to -∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy = -∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx. Hence the claimed limit (Filter.Tendsto.congr'). QED

proof_key_steps: margin: delta > 0 with K' := cthickening delta (tsupport tau) ⊆ U and h0 := delta/(||e|| + 1)
for 0 < |h| < h0 the integrand vanishes off U, so ∫_U = ∫_{R^n}; all pieces are continuous on the compact support, hence integrable
linearity and translation invariance give ∫_U F[h^{-1}(tau - tau(. - he))] = -∫_K h^{-1}(F(y + he) - F(y))[tau(y)] dy
sibling diffquot_uniform (E = L*): h^{-1}(F(y + he) - F(y)) -> DF(y)e uniformly on K
bounded integrands on the finite-measure K: dominated convergence gives the limit -∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] = -∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)]
